summary: This MR adds a new API endpoint for retrieving favorite products. The configuration changes (API Platform XML definitions and serialization groups) follow Symfony/API Platform conventions. The code is straightforward configuration with no logical implementation changes visible. Overall the changes are minimal and follow existing patterns in the codebase.

issues.description: The new endpoint is missing explicit access control (security) configuration. Other endpoints in the file likely have security attributes that should be consistent.
issues.fix: Add security attribute to restrict access. Example: <attribute name="security">is_granted('ROLE_USER')</attribute>

issues.description: Pagination is disabled with a comment but no explanation for why. If this is intentional (e.g., small dataset), consider documenting the business rationale.
issues.fix: Either remove the comment or add a more descriptive comment explaining why pagination is disabled for this specific endpoint

issues.description: The serialization group naming is inconsistent. Existing groups use 'app:shop:product:search' while new groups use 'app:shop:product:favorites'. Verify this follows the project's naming convention.
issues.fix: No change needed if this is consistent with project conventions. Otherwise, align with existing naming patterns.

suggestions: Verify that the new endpoint has proper security configuration to ensure only authorized users can access favorites
Consider if there are any performance implications of disabling pagination for the favorites endpoint
Ensure the new endpoint is properly documented in the API documentation
Check if there are controller/provider classes that need to be implemented or modified to support this new endpoint
Verify that the serialization groups include all necessary fields for the favorites use case (not too much or too little data)
Consider adding integration tests for the new favorites endpoint
